items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I see Nick Brignola at Ithaca College with Reece Markowitz, they all got noticed

ctx.x: I have to say no, but I auditioned for Fredonia first. That’s where I wanted to go because I knew that Don Menza and Sam Noto — or Don Menza had gone there. And there’s a bass player named Linc Milliman who played bass — Linc was basically from six miles outside of Mount Morris is where he grew up, so I used to play with his father, his mother and his sisters and with Linc. And I knew they went to Fredonia so I auditioned for Fredonia but they turned me down because I couldn’t sight sing. You know they made me,…

did not want me, made it difficult for me. And then there was an opening in the wind ensemble and Joe Roccisano, I don’t know if you know Joe, Joe was a great saxophone player. Joe was going to school at the time and he auditioned me on tenor to go into the wind ensemble, and he said, “Yeah, that’s good. You’ll pass. You can go in.” And my clarinet teacher balked and said, “No I don’t want him in the wind ensemble.” So with that animosity I only lasted one semester. And you know jazz was not — you know the school…
Well if it’ll make you feel any better regarding Fredonia, Don Menza told me when he was at Fredonia he said practicing bebop was a felony, practicing Dixieland was just a misdemeanor.
